articleText: Anthropic's internal AI use is now worth more than employee pay, at the prices it charges customers Business Insider
reactions: [Hacker News] I have thought of this and I think if you have value you can gain by adding more directing power (a person) then yes. Get another person to unlock that token spend on creating value. Otherwise, don’t hire that person as existing resources can direct that token spend. If you have no where to grow, adding another person will not benefit from more token spend.

[Hacker News] There's unfortunately a lot of emotions and cope around this so you will be downvoted. There was a recent viral news article implying that Anthropic had lost 80B in a single quarter, this was really because of increased valuations. But a lot still believe this is the case and Anthropic will continue to have this 80B loss.. The reality is that they are profitable in the normal sense

[Hacker News] Xerox made quite a bit of money selling laser printers for desktop publishing, too, a lot more than they ever spent on PARC. I don't think it's accurate that "almost all the money in personal computing was made in mobile". Quite a bit of money was made in personal computing before the iPhone, and quite a bit of money has been made in non-mobile computing since the iPhone. I als
[Hacker News] I'm not really following. My point here is that this is why the ceiling is around 20x, as opposed to being e.g. 200x or 2,000x. That doesn't mean it's "much lower than 5x."
[Hacker News] I don't disagree that they pay more, but how much more? The value/usage of a $100 sub is also fairly opaque and perpetually decreasing...

[Hacker News] No, I deliberately don't own stock in the companies I write about (or any single companies at all, aside from a Vanguard index fund.) I've learned enough that I am confident that enterprise companies pay a lot more for their tokens than $100/month subscribers, and that negotiated enterprise discounts don't change that fact in a meaningful way.
